scorecards.inningsCommentary: New Zealand commenced their first innings at Sheikh Zayed Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 63 from Kane Williamson, complemented by a commanding 72-run stand between HM Nicholls and Kane Williamson that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.3 RPO. Pakistan's bowling response was spearheaded by Yasir Shah (3/54), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Folded for 153/10 (66.3 ov), New Zealand suffered an early setback, conceding vital first-innings momentum to Pakistan.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sheikh Zayed Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as New Zealand posted 153/10 (66.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Pakistan countered with 227/10 (83.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: AY Patel (6/59), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, AY Patel delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (12 Runs & 8 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (New Zealand 48%) and allowing New Zealand to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Pakistan faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. New Zealand's bowling unit, bolstered by Yasir Shah (9 Runs & 8 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing New Zealand won by 4 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: New Zealand's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Pakistan produced fighting phases, New Zealand won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
